question: Which lesser-known contractors, testers and insurers sit underneath the big national-security tech programs?
answer: The science plan's structural map names 48 firm entries (45 different names; a few firms sit in more than one corridor), and 19 kinds of firm, beneath the headline programs in 8 corridors. In AI compute: WWT, SambaNova and the engineers Bridgers & Paxton, Burns & McDonnell and Sargent & Lundy. On the grid: study and test firms such as Qualus, PowerGEM, Doble and Shermco. In quantum and encryption: Bluefors, FormFactor, Entrust and SafeLogic. In minerals and nuclear: SRK, NAC International and the insurer-engineer FM Approvals. 46 of the 48 entries match a row in an NSSTS registry (by name, or by row id where no name matched). The map says these firms do not inherit final authority, and it cites no source per corridor.

package_synthesis — the page cites no sources per corridor; most named firms are rows in the NSSTS hidden-tier registries (pivotal third party, hidden supply chain, hidden referee, transaction trigger, quantum-cryptographic acceptance)

Registry rows are joined by name, or by row id where no name matched (each card's 'Matched on' line); a match on a family name such as 'Intertek' or 'FM' may be a sibling entity, and at most two matching rows are shown per name.

4 of the seven hidden-tier registries are marked pending workbench evidence: NSSTS Hidden Acceptance Economy Registry; NSSTS Hidden Referee and Decision-Record Deep-Dive Registry; NSSTS Quantum and Cryptographic Acceptance Registry; NSSTS Transaction, Failure and Return-to-Service Trigger Registry. research.answer: This study maps which exact companies could supply, test, finance or run the projects behind the National Security Science and Technology Strategy across twelve tech sectors.

research.title: Winning a federal tech award is not the same as being accepted
research.answer: Across ten federal technology programs, the study finds that awards, production and prototypes still fall short of the government actually accepting a working system. Being near a program is not being in it.

research.title: What it takes for quantum tech and new encryption to win federal approval
research.answer: A federal agency does not accept a quantum device or post-quantum encryption because a vendor says it works. It needs a chain of separate proofs ending in a named official's sign-off, and most companies are still partway down that chain.
